Realities.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib, which carries full local symbols and one process function per model. Realities::process is at 0x125f0. The six CV jacks all scale by a fifth of a volt except the modulation rate (a tenth) and depth (a twentieth), each matched to a knob that is itself scaled, so 5V covers the whole travel in every case. Freeze and Reverse are latches: the button toggles on each press and the jack exclusive-ors with it, so a held gate inverts the button rather than overriding it. Gen calls srand with the current time and redraws the random diffuser lengths. What the colour control filters was not traced past its clamp, so its line says only that it sets the colour. The Type parameter, index 4, is configured with five positions and read in process but has no ParamWidget, so it cannot be clicked, turned or tagged.

Mist.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Mist::process is at 0xdefc. The distribution switch is off by one against its own labels. At 0xdf80 the code takes the jack's voltage times 1.2, subtracts 1, and adds the truncated switch value; with nothing patched the jack reads 0V, so the number handed to Distribution::process is the switch position minus one, clamped to 0 at the bottom. Distribution::process at 0x884c subtracts 1 again and dispatches 1 to 5 as Cauchy, logistic, hyperbolic, arcsine and exponential, with everything else falling through to a uniform draw. So UNI and CAUCHY both give the uniform shape, LOGIST gives Cauchy, HYPERBCOS gives logistic, ARCSINE gives hyperbolic, EXP gives arcsine and DUST gives exponential. The seven label strings are built inline in Mist::Mist at 0xd130 as UNI, CAUCHY, LOGIST, HYPERBCOS, ARCSINE, EXP and DUST. Output 0 is configured but has no PortWidget and is never written, so it gets no line and no tag; output 1 is the only jack on the panel. The rate figure of one to twenty thousand a second is 20000 raised to the knob's own 0 to 1 range, from the constant 0x469C4000 at 0xdf34; the hundred and forty a second at the default half-travel follows from it.

Lucid.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Lucid::process is at 0xaacc and drives VoltageControlledOscillator<16,16,simd::Vector<float,4>>::process at 0xacbc, four channels at a time. Polyphony is real and not an isConnected test: 0xaaf0 takes the pitch jack's channel count and 0xab0c uses it as the loop bound. The pitch knob is configured -48 to 48 with a display base of the twelfth root of two and a multiplier of 261.6256, so it is semitones around C4 and reads out in Hz; process divides it by twelve before adding the pitch jack. Rise and fall are each 0.025 to 0.2 of a cycle and are handed to the oscillator as the four corners of a trapezoid. The tilt, rise and fall jacks are read on channel 0 only and applied to every channel. The FM knob is squared with its sign kept, which is why small settings move the pitch so little. What the tilt control changes inside the oscillator beyond doubling into a 0 to 1 shape control was not traced further.

Adrift.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Adrift::process is at 0x2b40. The tempo knob is configured -2 to 4 with a display base of 2 and a multiplier of 60, so 15 to 960 beats per minute with 120 at the default. The register is a single byte shifted left on each clock. The seven stage outputs are bits 0 to 6 of the register before the shift; index order is bottom to top on the panel, output 0 being the lowest jack. Output 7 is the byte itself scaled by ten divided by 255. The threshold on the +1 jack depends on the Pulse Mode setting: 2V and edge-triggered in one mode, 1V and level-sensitive in the other. Pulse Mode and its two choices Gate and Trig are read from AdriftWidget::appendContextMenu at 0x4240, where the item name is a literal and the two choice names are built inline. The button parameter has no name configured, so nothing but this entry describes it.

Wander.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Two faults, both checkable. First, three of the four jacks are dead: process loads the inputs pointer once at 0x170a0 and reads offset 0 only, so the coherence, duration and duration-coherence jacks are configured, drawn on the panel and never read. Second, the five outputs are each one distribution away from the name on the jack. Distribution::process at 0x884c subtracts one from the number it is given before dispatching, so 1 to 5 are Cauchy, logistic, hyperbolic, arcsine and exponential and anything else falls through to a uniform draw; the jump table at 0x1dfb6 confirms that order. Wander calls it with 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 for the five outputs, at 0x17180, 0x171f4, 0x17268, 0x172d8 and 0x17348. The result is that the Cauchy jack carries a uniform draw and the exponential distribution never appears on any jack. The same function is called once more, at 0x173ac, with the duration switch's own value, and that call is not shifted, which is what says the five output calls are the ones that are wrong. The rate knob is configured 0.01 to 20 but 0x170b4 clamps it at 4, so four fifths of its travel does nothing; the step length can still push the rate above 4 afterwards. Both coherence controls are named for different distributions but only the amplitude one is used: 0x170e8 loads it and it is the shape parameter for all six draws, including the duration one.

Moment.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Moment::process is at 0xfacc. The colour jack, input 3, is dead: the function reads input offsets 0, 0x50, 0xa0, 0x140, 0x190 and 0x1e0 and never 0xf0. The delay rate is half the clock rate times two raised to 9.9658 minus 13.2876 times the time knob plus the time jack, so a volt at the time jack doubles or halves the delay and the knob spans 1ms to 10 seconds; the configured display base of 10000 and multiplier of 0.001 agree, and the default of 0.6747 gives exactly half a second at the 2Hz base rate. The clock input is measured edge to edge and only accepted between 0.001Hz and 1000Hz. The filter in the feedback path is a one-pole lowpass whose corner is 100 raised to twice the colour knob minus one, times 20000, clamped to 39Hz and 11000Hz. Reverse is a latch: the button toggles on each press and the jack exclusive-ors with it.

Loom.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.1.0 plugin.dylib. Loom::process is at 0x832c. Both signals are mapped to unsigned 16-bit numbers, combined with exclusive-or and with and, mapped back to -1 to 1 and put through a one-pole lowpass at 11kHz before the output; the exclusive-or and multiplying outputs also go through a hyperbolic tangent, the and output does not. The frequency knob is configured -8 to 12 with a display base of 2, so two raised to that, and process adds the pitch jack to it before the power of two. The internal oscillator is a sine: its mode field at 0x178 is set to zero in the constructor and LFO::process at 0x85c8 dispatches zero to sinf. The two exclusive-or and and paths share one filter state, so each interferes slightly with the other.
